removability.rationale: Deleting the feature means several scattered edits inside one 878-line file plus a CSS cleanup; nothing is entangled across modules, but features are not module-isolated, so removal is a grep exercise, not a delete-a-file operation.

app/src/main.js:156 — home list, and app/src/main.js:685,715,767 — move/ability/type lists all render through pokemonCardListHtml (app/src/ui.js:30)

changeability.rationale: The named bug and most data fixes land in exactly one helper covering every consumer. Deducted one point because badge markup is duplicated four times, so a badge change means five edits.

evidence: app/server.mjs:25-35 — server only injects window.__API_BASE_URL__ and serves files; all rendering is client-side
app/src/api.js:15-20 — resolveApiUrl is the single place that knows the /api/v2/ prefix

coupling.rationale: Clean one-way layering (api → data/ui → main), narrow interfaces, explicit config injection, no global mutable state beyond the render token. Minor tangles: media-URL knowledge sits in the HTTP module and home-page filter state is mutated inside a closure.

evidence: app/src/ui.js:27-32 — optionsForSpecies callback handles the real variation (types on home, hidden-ability badge) without flag parameters
app/src/main.js:651-652 — detailsPanelHtml is a trivial one-use wrapper
app/src/main.js:655-780 — each page is a bespoke render function; no page/section abstraction to plug an Items section into
app/src/ui.js:12 — typeBadge doesn't stretch to linked badges, hence the four inline copies
abstraction_design.rationale: The shared abstractions (card, panel, ref→species helpers) are well shaped for the app's actual variation, but they stop short of a page-level abstraction: a new section means copying a render function, and small helpers show copy-paste or one-off drift.

findings.issue: Router, all eight pages' rendering, and all event handling live in a single 878-line module; features cannot be added or removed by touching or deleting one file.
findings.suggestion: Split into per-page modules (e.g. src/pages/home.js, pokemon.js, moves.js, ...) with a small router that imports and dispatches to them.

findings.issue: Type-badge link markup is duplicated inline four times (main.js:361, 584, 678, 751) while ui.js exports a span-only typeBadge that main.js imports but never uses.
findings.suggestion: Extend typeBadge to emit a link when given an href (or add a typeBadgeLink helper) and use it from all five sites; drop the dead import.

findings.issue: The '<count> Pokémon' + card-list panel pattern is repeated in three renderers (685, 712-718, 767) with slight variations.
findings.suggestion: Add a pokemonListPanelHtml(id, title, species) helper in ui.js so the count text, list, and panel markup change in one place.

findings.issue: Caching exists in two layers: the response cache in api.js:11 and per-entity promise memoization in data.js, so a change to caching rules (TTL, invalidation) touches both files and three memoized variables.
findings.suggestion: Route the data.js memoization through a single memoize helper in api.js (or add an option on api()) so caching policy has one home.

findings.issue: Home-page filter state is a mutable object captured in a closure, with two render paths: partial innerHTML on input/change (131-167) and a full renderRoute re-render on pagination links, which reloads and rebuilds everything.
findings.suggestion: Make filter state derivable from the URL only and re-render through one path (still fine to keep partial DOM updates, but let the URL be the single source of truth).

findings.issue: spriteUrl bakes the media path (/media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png) into the HTTP/fetch module, which is otherwise data-source agnostic.
findings.suggestion: Move sprite/media URL construction to ui.js or a small media.js so api.js stays purely about fetching and formatting API data.

findings.issue: detailsPanelHtml is a one-line wrapper used exactly once, adding indirection without abstraction.

summary: Well-layered for a framework-free app: one shared card component covers every Pokémon list, all HTTP and caching goes through a single api.js seam, and server/client code are cleanly separated, so the sprite-bug scenario is a one-file fix. The main cost is the monolithic 878-line main.js holding the router and every page's rendering and handlers, which turns feature removal and new sections into grep-and-edit work. Smaller duplication (type-badge markup ×5, the count+list panel pattern ×3, two caching layers) is findable but will bite anyone changing shared markup or data-source policy.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Delete renderAbility (690-726) and the route branch (807), plus the Abilities panel and /abilities links inside renderPokemon (639-643) and .hidden-ability CSS (styles.css:259). No cross-module entanglement, but everything is inside main.js and the extraHtml card option becomes dead, so it's four scattered edits rather than deleting a module.

scenarios.change: Fix wrong card sprite for species whose default Pokémon has a different name (e.g. Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: Cards are built in one place (ui.js:21 via spriteUrl in api.js:84) and every list — home (main.js:156), move (685), ability (715), type (767) — renders through pokemonCardListHtml, so a single fix covers all of them. Note the app derives sprites from the species ID, which matches the documented /media/sprites/pokemon/<id>.png pattern, so it likely renders correctly today.

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: Move/ability/type lists all flow through speciesIdsFromPokemonRefs/speciesRefsByIds (data.js:90-105), so one sort there covers three; the home page has its own filter/slice pipeline over speciesData.refs (main.js:131-167) that must be edited separately. Sorting by English (not humanized API) names would also require loading species details, which the current species refs don't carry.

scenarios.change: Add an Items section (/items, /items/:name) shaped like Moves
scenarios.notes: api(), panelHtml, setPage, the render-token guard, not-found handling and the router's dispatch are reusable, but there is no page-level abstraction: the item detail/list pages are ~80 lines copied in shape from renderMove/renderTypeList inside main.js, plus new CSS. Reuse is of generic helpers, not of the Moves code itself.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: Base URL is a deliberate seam: server.mjs:8 reads the env and injects one global that api.js:1-4 consumes; a base-URL change alone is two coordinated places. Caching, however, lives in two layers — responseCache in api.js:11 and memoized species/types/generations promises in data.js:11-13 — so changing cache policy (TTL, invalidation) means editing both files.
